# `jouet stack sync`

- **Usage:** `jouet stack sync [FLAGS] [BRANCH]`

Bring each layer up to date by merging its parent, verified, never rebasing

Fetches, then goes up the stack from the bottom. Each layer starts from its local branch, never the remote's, so unpushed fixes are kept; a local branch behind its remote is refused. A layer that lacks its parent gets the parent merged in, or the trunk once its prerequisite has merged (a squash merge included). Each merge is checked before it is committed: every change it brings in must be in the merged tree. Sync stops at the first layer that conflicts, fails that check, is checked out in another worktree, or has uncommitted changes, and says what to do. A branch checked out nowhere is merged in a temporary worktree; the one checked out here is merged in place. Never rebases or force-pushes; pushes only with --push, plainly. Exits 1 on a conflict or a failed check, 4 when refused before merging, 5 when a fetch or push fails.

## Arguments
- **`[BRANCH]`** — A branch in the stack (default: the current branch)

## Flags
- **`--dry-run`** — Show what would be merged; merge, fetch and push nothing
- **`--push`** — Push the layers ahead of their remote branch afterwards (never forced)
- **`--no-fetch`** — Use the remote branches as last fetched
- **`-h --help`** — Print help
